Package io.mavlink4j.service

Class ManualControlService

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.service.ManualControlService
public final class ManualControlService extends Object
MAVLink's manual-control microservice (Family B — streaming, see docs/API.md): a fixed-rate RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE (#70) relay, latest-wins mailbox, no acknowledgement at all, run on this module's own TxScheduler instead of a hand-rolled per-link thread.

ISP: this class cannot express an ack wait

Constructed from FrameSink + TxScheduler + PeerDirectory only — no Correlator. Manual control is genuinely fire-and-forget on the wire (the spec defines no rate and no failsafe-on-silence for RC override); giving this class a way to await a reply would let a future change quietly grow a request/response dependency where the protocol has none.

Two rates, not one: a ceiling and a keepalive

A single fixed rate used to serve as both "how often we transmit" and "how long a new stick position waits", which cost a frame up to a full period of dead time for no protocol reason. The rate is now split:
  • coalescePeriod (1/maxOverrideHz) — the wire ceiling. Never transmit faster than this, however fast the caller writes.
  • keepalivePeriod (1/clampedOverrideHz) — the wire floor. An unchanged mailbox still transmits this often, so an aircraft never sees a gap long enough to expire its own override timeout.
A write that arrives at least coalescePeriod after the last transmit is pushed to the wire immediately, via a one-shot, instead of waiting for the next tick. The periodic task therefore stops being the send loop and becomes the keepalive: it transmits only when the mailbox is dirty or the floor is due, so the combined wire rate is bounded by the ceiling rather than being the sum of the two paths.

Re-resolution every tick, never cached

A peer's sourceAddress refreshes on every inbound datagram and can change at any time (a NAT rebind, a relay taking over). Every ManualControlService.RcLinkRuntime tick re-reads PeerDirectory.peer(io.mavlink4j.PeerId) fresh; caching the target at engage(io.mavlink4j.PeerId) would let the sender keep transmitting to a stale address after the vehicle moves. A tick that finds the target currently unknown pauses — logged once on the transition, not fatal and not a busy-spin.

Every channel 1..16 the caller populates reaches the wire

Channels 9..16 (MAVLink's "extension" channels) are never silently forced to RcChannels.IGNORE: ManualControlService.RcLinkRuntime.buildFrame(io.mavlink4j.service.RcChannels) populates every channel from the mailbox via RcChannels.wireValue(int), which also resolves the extension-channel sentinel asymmetry (channels 9..16 use 65534 for release, not the 0 channels 1..8 use). Channels 17/18 are always RcChannels.IGNORE — ArduPilot does not read them, and RcChannels itself refuses to carry a value there.

    • ManualControlService

      public ManualControlService(FrameSink sink, TxScheduler scheduler, PeerDirectory peers, MavlinkSettings settings)
      Rates come from MavlinkSettings.rc(): the ceiling is 1/maxOverrideHz, the keepalive 1/clampedOverrideHz, the release burst releaseFrames. Time is read from MavlinkSettings.clock(), so a test steps it by hand.

  • Method Details

    • engage

      public ManualControlService.ManualControlLink engage(PeerId target)
      Starts a fixed-rate relay to target. Fails fast, starting no periodic task at all, if target has never been heard from — "you cannot command what you cannot hear" (the same reachability rule RoutingFrameSink enforces on every send).
      Throws:
      PeerUnreachableException - if target is not (yet) known to PeerDirectory

    • send

      public void send(ManualControlService.ManualControlLink link, RcChannels channels)
      Overwrites link's latest-wins mailbox with channels and, when the wire ceiling has already elapsed, schedules an immediate one-shot transmit rather than letting the frame wait for the next tick (see the class javadoc's two-rates section). Non-blocking, and it still never touches the wire on the caller's own thread; a silent no-op once link has begun releasing.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if link was not created by this service's own engage(io.mavlink4j.PeerId)

    • release

      public CompletableFuture<Void> release(ManualControlService.ManualControlLink link)
      Writes an all-RcChannels.RELEASE frame into link's mailbox and returns at once. The still-ticking relay transmits the releaseFrames-frame burst on the TxScheduler, then stops itself; the returned future completes when that burst has been handed to the sink (or dropped because the target became unreachable). A caller that must not proceed until the burst is out waits on the future — nothing in this class does. Idempotent: a second release on an already-releasing link returns the same future.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if link was not created by this service's own engage(io.mavlink4j.PeerId)
